One opera tradition (Qinqiang) spans Shaanxi; Gansu and Ningxia. Guanzhong was the Qin; Han; Sui and Tang capital region - the classic base from which China gets unified. GAINS QINGHAI AT MAP B1 (and at B3 on the other branch).

SOVEREIGN ON MAPS A AND B2. Merges into The Northwest at B1 and stays merged thereafter. B1 and B2 are parallel branches - the chronological order of this merge against the Mongol one is NOT ESTABLISHED. The most plural first-order unit in the survey - Han 50.5-54%; Tibetan 20.7-21%; Hui 16%; Tu 4%. Deliberately colored as a lighter kin of The Northwest so the reader sees the merge coming; the same trick used for Mongolia and Inner Mongolia. Never Tibetan: giving it to Tibet would have cut Tibet from 86.0% to 45.6% Tibetan.

THE LARGEST OF THE HAN STATES at ~260 million; and the most persistent breakaway in Chinese history - Shu; Shu Han; Cheng Han; Former Shu; Later Shu; and a de facto independent warlord Sichuan into the 1930s. Ringed by mountains with the Qinling sealing it from the north.

notes: Shanxi alone. Northern Han (capital Taiyuan) in the Ten Kingdoms and Yan Xishan's Shanxi clique in the Warlord Era - the same single province becoming a state twice; a thousand years apart. Yan Xishan kept Shanxi on a deliberately different railroad gauge from the rest of China.

Wuyue (capital Hangzhou) in the Ten Kingdoms. ABSORBS JIANGHUAI - Jiangsu and Anhui are Mandarin-speaking ground that Skinner places in the same macroregion as Wu; so they are folded in rather than drawn as a separate state. That makes Wu the industrial core: Shanghai; Baosteel and the two largest ports.
Jiangxi. Corresponds cleanly to one province; which is rare here.
Hunan. Chu (capital Changsha) in the Ten Kingdoms; Hunan warlords in the 1920s.

Min (capital Fuzhou) in the Ten Kingdoms. Min is five languages compressed into one state - splitting it five ways would give Fujian more weight than the entire north. THE ONLY BRANCH THAT SPANS THE STRAIT; which is why Taiwan is a live question in every era.

NEVER JOINS THE FEDERATION. Draw the TIAN SHAN as an INTERNAL DASHED LINE on every map - it separates the 95% non-Han Tarim from Han- and Kazakh-majority Dzungaria; and the whole-subdivision rule forbids making it a border. Label TARIM and DZUNGARIA either side.

THE TIBET AUTONOMOUS REGION AND NOTHING ELSE; on all eight maps. It never gains Qinghai. 86% Tibetan with the lowest intermarriage rates in China. Holds the headwaters of the Yellow; Yangtze; Mekong; Salween; Brahmaputra and Indus.

Sovereign on all eight maps. Note the tension: Skinner puts Taiwan inside the Southeast Coast macroregion and Taiwanese IS coastal Southern Min; so the tidiest reading would be a Min province. It is drawn separate on the strength of the hybridity finding and fifty years of Japanese institutions.
